version.changelog: feat: real-time hospital list fetch from backend API; no longer depends on bundled JSON data

llm.summary: This booking skill has a coherent purpose, but it needs review because it can submit sensitive appointment details and open browser URLs in ways that are not safely controlled.

dimensions.detail: Declared network endpoints are mostly related to booking and pricing, but api/browser/open-url.js uses child_process.exec with an interpolated URL after only hostname validation, creating a command-injection risk if a remote or context-provided clinic URL contains shell metacharacters.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package has no npm lifecycle install hooks, but the README uses unpinned npx and remote installer commands. Developer scripts can copy the skill into local agent session directories or restart OpenClaw services, but these scripts are not wired into the normal package install path.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The manifest says contact data is sent only after explicit consent, but runtime intent detection can submit when a clinic context exists and the user mentions a date or headcount; it also logs parsed form data and full payloads. A hidden HTML comment is used to pass clinic context, which appears purpose-aligned but should be disclosed as state handling.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No runtime system persistence or broad filesystem permission was found in the main skill; it declares filesystem false. Persistence-like behavior is limited to conversational clinic context plus optional developer scripts that manually modify local skill caches if run.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Clinic lookup, price lookup, browser opening, and appointment submission match the stated BeautsGO booking purpose, but direct booking is a real-world action involving phone numbers and medical-aesthetic preferences, and the implementation does not reliably require a final explicit confirmation before submission.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with the skill contacting BeautsGO-related services and sending appointment details such as clinic, date, party size, and contact information. Before approval, require a fix for the unsafe browser opener, remove or redact PII logs, add a clear final confirmation before every booking submission, and prefer pinned install instructions.
llm.findings:
[AE1] unexpected: Overridden for this adjudication: the referenced entry file artifact/api/skill.js was locally available and inspected.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted: the URL opener uses shell exec with the original URL string, so allowed-host validation does not prevent command injection through URL path, query, or fragment content.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted: appointment data can be logged and submitted without a dedicated consent state or final confirmation, despite the privacy claim that data is sent only after explicit consent.
[E1] expected: External calls to BeautsGO and related pricing APIs are expected for a booking and price-query skill, but transmission of contact and appointment details needs stronger user confirmation and minimization.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted in part: collecting contact details is expected, but the examples and runtime do not make the consent checkpoint prominent or enforce it before API submission.
[SC4] unexpected: Downgraded: the flagged vulnerable dependencies appear in dev/test tooling rather than the core runtime dependency path, but they should still be updated before publication.
[PE3] unexpected: Downgraded: the publish script mentions an Access Token shown by the CLI; it does not read local credential stores, though it should avoid encouraging token handling in plain terminal output.
[P2] unexpected: Downgraded: the reviewed HTML comments are section labels and reporting annotations, not hidden agent instructions.
[RP1] unexpected: Accepted as a supply-chain hygiene issue: install examples use floating npx or remote references without pinning, which can install content different from the reviewed artifact.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted as documentation mismatch: some text says automatic clicking, while code opens pages or submits backend requests, which can mislead users about what action is being taken.
